column1: # GE-T10's third question set (SMYSL-2.5 OQ-22's owed spelling fixes, and subject morphology):
# sixteen questions, two per intent, each asked in the five tier-1 languages, eighty rows, over
# the committed corpus (`../gold/corpus.smy`). Only the front is scored on it — the intent the
# table reads and the subject the entity port finds — so it has no slot gold.
# WHY A THIRD SET. Sets 1 and 2 found two kinds of loss: spellings the intent table does not
# write, and inflected subjects no exact match can meet. A fix measured on the questions that
# found it is measured in-sample, so both fixes are scored here, on questions written before
# either fix was made, and the figures before the fixes were taken on it first (`baseline.txt`,
# written by the harness before the code changed). The fixes were declared before any run of this set:
#   1. a comma after the rule's verb is not part of the rule (`wer sagte, …`, `stimmt es, dass`)
#   3. plural verbs where the table has the singular (`wo werden … erwähnt`, `woher kommen`)
#   5. a stemmed match for a subject no exact spelling finds (Snowball, the question's language)
# WHO WROTE THIS. The same hand that wrote the fixes, which is the limit this set cannot remove:
# it knew which four spellings were to be fixed. The questions are written as a person would
# ask them — inflections, possessives, other verbs and other tenses kept — and several are
# expected to fail in ways no declared fix touches (`¿Quién fue …`, `Кем был …`, `Gibt es
# Belege …`, a surname without its forename, a German compound). Nothing was rephrased after a
# run. Single hand, so no agreement figure.
# Columns as `../gold/questions.tsv`: qid, intent, lang, question. The qid's prefix names the
# subject, as in GE-T10's SUBJECTS table.
